title: Pushout joins with a weak equivalence are right anodyne
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. For simplicial sets $X,Y$ define their ordered join by $(X\star Y)_n=X_n\amalg Y_n\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=n}X_a\times Y_b$, with $a,b\geq0$; simplicial operators restrict the initial block of $X$-vertices and final block of $Y$-vertices, with empty blocks giving the pure-factor summands. Let $i:A_0\hookrightarrow A$ and $j:B_0\hookrightarrow B$ be degreewise injective inclusions of small simplicial sets, and assume that $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then the canonical inclusion
$$
(A_0\star B)\amalg_{A_0\star B_0}(A\star B_0)\hookrightarrow A\star B
$$
is right anodyne. The displayed domain is the degreewise union of the two indicated simplicial subsets of $A\star B$, whose intersection is $A_0\star B_0$; equivalently it is their simplicial pushout. No Kan or quasicategory hypothesis is imposed on the four simplicial sets.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5 (Joyal), printed p. 251, PDF page 269. No Stacks tag: this is a simplicial right-anodyne join lemma.

proof.text: Write $\theta(i,j):D(i,j)\hookrightarrow A\star B$, with $D(i,j)=(A_0\star B)\cup(A\star B_0)$. By the ordered join formula, in degree $r$ this subset contains the pure summands $A_r$ and $B_r$, and in each mixed summand $A_u\times B_v$ it contains precisely $(A_{0,u}\times B_v)\cup(A_u\times B_{0,v})$. The intersection of the two joined subsets is $A_0\star B_0$, on pure as well as mixed summands. Thus their degreewise union is the stated pushout: a pair of simplicial maps agreeing on the intersection gives the unique map on the union. More generally all simplicial pushouts and ordinal colimits are computed degreewise: the set-theoretic quotient or colimit inherits its operators from those of the diagram, and compatible maps out of it are precisely natural transformations. This follows directly from the functor definition of simplicial sets in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Let $R$ denote the class in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Fix either variable of $\theta$, and let $\mathcal C$ be the class of monomorphisms in the other variable whose $\theta$ belongs to $R$. An isomorphism in either variable makes $\theta$ an isomorphism, because the mixed subset of Step 1 is then the whole product. A square of maps in either variable induces a square of $\theta$-maps: on mixed summands it applies the two coordinate maps, and on pure summands the corresponding single coordinate map. Identities and compositions hold coordinatewise and therefore also on $D$. Consequently an arrow retract in either variable induces an arrow retract of $\theta$. Thus $\mathcal C$ contains all isomorphisms and is retract closed. The map in a retract is still a monomorphism: apply the source section, cancel in the larger injection and then apply the source retraction.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Fix $j$. Push out $i:A_0\hookrightarrow A$ along $A_0\to A'_0$, giving $i':A'_0\hookrightarrow A'=A\amalg_{A_0}A'_0$. Degreewise $A'_u$ is the disjoint union of $A'_{0,u}$ and $A_u\setminus A_{0,u}$. The natural square from $\theta(i,j)$ to $\theta(i',j)$ is a pushout: the new elements in its top row are exactly $(A_u\setminus A_{0,u})\times(B_v\setminus B_{0,v})$, and its bottom row adds precisely the same elements. Its pure summands are already in the domains. The bijections are induced by the square, so commute with simplicial operators. Hence $\theta(i',j)$ is a pushout of $\theta(i,j)$ and belongs to $R$ whenever the latter does. For the second variable, push out $B_0\hookrightarrow B$ along $B_0\to B'_0$; then $B'_v=B'_{0,v}\amalg(B_v\setminus B_{0,v})$, and the same argument with new pairs $(A_u\setminus A_{0,u})\times(B_v\setminus B_{0,v})$ proves pushout closure in that variable too. Both pushed-out maps remain degreewise injective.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Fix $j:B_0\hookrightarrow B$ and a continuous chain of monomorphisms $X_0\hookrightarrow\cdots\hookrightarrow X_\lambda$. Each stage embeds in the colimit: equality in a set colimit over an ordinal is witnessed at a common later stage, where injectivity cancels it. Thus identify stages with subsets of $X_\lambda$. Put $P_\alpha=(X_\alpha\star B)\cup(X_\lambda\star B_0)$. Its intersection with $X_{\alpha+1}\star B$ is $(X_\alpha\star B)\cup(X_{\alpha+1}\star B_0)$ and its union with that joined subset is $P_{\alpha+1}$, by Step 1. Therefore $P_\alpha\hookrightarrow P_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout of $\theta(X_\alpha\hookrightarrow X_{\alpha+1},j)$. At a nonzero limit $\delta$, every mixed simplex involving $X_\delta$ has its first coordinate in some earlier stage, while $X_\lambda\star B_0$ is present at every stage. Hence $P_\delta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\delta}P_\alpha$. This continuous chain starts at $D(X_0\hookrightarrow X_\lambda,j)$ and ends at $X_\lambda\star B$. If all successor $\theta$-maps belong to $R$, its composite belongs to $R$ by transfinite-composition and pushout closure. The zero-length chain gives an identity.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: For the other variable, fix $i:A_0\hookrightarrow A$ and a continuous chain of inclusions $Y_\alpha\subseteq Y_\lambda$. Put $Q_\alpha=(A\star Y_\alpha)\cup(A_0\star Y_\lambda)$. Then $Q_\alpha\cap(A\star Y_{\alpha+1})=(A\star Y_\alpha)\cup(A_0\star Y_{\alpha+1})$, and their union is $Q_{\alpha+1}$. Thus $Q_\alpha\hookrightarrow Q_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout of $\theta(i,Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y_{\alpha+1})$. At a nonzero limit the second coordinate of a mixed simplex occurs at some earlier stage, so $Q_\delta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\delta}Q_\alpha$. The endpoints are $D(i,Y_0\hookrightarrow Y_\lambda)$ and $A\star Y_\lambda$. Closure of $R$ again proves transfinite-composition closure in the second variable. Together with Steps 2 and 3, the class $\mathcal C$ for either fixed variable contains isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Each class $\mathcal C$ of Step 2 is also closed under small coproducts of its maps. Indeed, well-order a family $f_t:U_t\hookrightarrow V_t$ in $\mathcal C$. Starting with $\coprod_tU_t$, replace the $t$th summand by $V_t$ in that order. The successor map is a pushout of $f_t$ along the summand inclusion, every limit is the degreewise colimit, and the final object is $\coprod_tV_t$. Thus the coproduct map is a transfinite composite of pushouts of the $f_t$, so lies in $\mathcal C$ by Steps 3--5. The empty family gives an identity. Choose the well-order with small ordinal type in the fixed universe; every coproduct and chain used here is small.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Consider $i:\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ with $n\geq0$ and $j:\Lambda_k^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ with $m\geq1$ and $0\leq k\leq m$. There is a simplicial isomorphism $\Delta^n\star\Delta^m\cong\Delta^N$, $N=n+m+1$: a monotone map into $[N]$ splits uniquely into its initial block with values at most $n$ and its final block with values at least $n+1$; subtract $n+1$ on the second block. Empty blocks give the pure summands. Restricting a monotone map restricts these blocks, so this bijection commutes with all operators. Write $p=n+1+k$. Using the boundary definition (union of proper faces) in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], a mixed simplex lies in $\partial\Delta^n\star\Delta^m$ exactly when its image omits a first-block vertex, and in $\Delta^n\star\Lambda_k^m$ exactly when it omits a second-block vertex other than $p$. Hence the mixed simplices of $D(i,j)$ are exactly those omitting some vertex other than $p$. A pure second-block simplex omits a first-block vertex, since $n+1\geq1$. A pure first-block simplex omits a second-block vertex other than $p$, since $m+1\geq2$. Both pure factors therefore satisfy the same criterion. By the horn definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $D(i,j)$ is exactly $\Lambda_p^N$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Since $p=n+1+k\geq1$ and $p\leq n+1+m=N$, the map computed in Step 7 is a right horn generator of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. It therefore belongs to $R$. This includes $n=0$, $k=0$ and $k=m$; there is no restriction to inner horns.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Fix a boundary inclusion $i:\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. Steps 7--8 show that the class $\mathcal C_i$ of second-variable monomorphisms whose $\theta(i,-)$ belongs to $R$ contains every horn inclusion. Steps 2--6 make this class closed under pushouts, small coproducts, transfinite compositions and retracts. The statement of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] says that cofibrations are the monomorphisms and that trivial cofibrations are retracts of transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of horn inclusions. Consequently any degreewise injective weak homotopy equivalence $j$ lies in $\mathcal C_i$: it is a cofibration and a weak equivalence in exactly that model structure, hence a trivial cofibration, to which the stated horn-cell/retract description applies. The weak-equivalence notion there is realization-based, exactly the notion in the item; neither source nor target has to be Kan.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed p. 251, PDF page 269 (zero-based page 268); two saturation reductions and boundary-horn calculation. Read online; not archived locally. Degreewise details supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Now fix the given degreewise injective weak homotopy equivalence $j:B_0\hookrightarrow B$. Step 9 puts every boundary inclusion, including $\varnothing=\partial\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$, in the first-variable class $\mathcal C_j$. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], every monomorphism $i$ is a transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of boundary inclusions. The first-variable closure and coproduct arguments of Steps 2--6 therefore put $i$ in $\mathcal C_j$. Thus $\theta(i,j)$ is right anodyne. Step 1 identifies its domain with the displayed union and simplicial pushout, proving every clause of the statement.
